pages.summary: Make a new figure window, or bring one to the front and make it current.
body: Plots go into the current figure, made when the first plot needs one. `figure` starts another, so that the next plot does not replace the last; `figure(n)` makes figure `n` current, making it if it does not exist. Name-value pairs set the figure's properties, such as `'Name'`, `'Color'` and `'Position'` (`[left bottom width height]` in pixels).
syntax: A new figure, which becomes the current one.
Figure `n`, made if need be, as the current figure.
A new figure with properties set, and its handle.

examples.title: Two figures
examples.code:
x = linspace(0, 1, 50);
figure
plot(x, x.^2)
title('first')
figure
plot(x, sqrt(x))
title('second')

examples.title: A named figure of a chosen size

pages.summary: Axes in a grid of tiles within the figure.
body: `subplot(m, n, p)` divides the figure into `m` rows and `n` columns of tiles and makes tile `p` current, counting along the rows. Plots then go into that tile. A vector of tile numbers spans several tiles. Calling it again with the same tile returns to those axes.
syntax: One axes spanning the tiles listed.

examples.title: Four plots in a two-by-two grid
examples.code:
x = linspace(0, 2*pi, 100);
subplot(2, 2, 1)
plot(x, sin(x))
title('sin')
subplot(2, 2, 2)
plot(x, cos(x))
title('cos')
subplot(2, 2, 3)
plot(x, sin(2*x))
title('sin 2x')
subplot(2, 2, 4)
plot(x, cos(2*x))
title('cos 2x')

examples.title: A wide tile under two small ones
examples.code:
rng default
subplot(2, 2, 1)
histogram(randn(1, 500))
subplot(2, 2, 2)
scatter(rand(1, 30), rand(1, 30))
subplot(2, 2, [3 4])
plot(cumsum(randn(1, 200)))

pages.summary: A grid of tiles for axes, filled one tile at a time.
body: `tiledlayout(m, n)` divides the figure into a grid; each `nexttile` makes the axes of the next tile current, along the rows. `nexttile(k)` goes to tile `k`. With `'flow'` the grid grows to fit however many tiles are asked for.
syntax: A grid that rearranges itself as tiles are added.
The axes of the next tile.

examples.title: Three tiles in a row
examples.code:
t = linspace(0, 1, 100);
tiledlayout(1, 3)
nexttile
plot(t, t)
title('linear')
nexttile
plot(t, t.^2)
title('square')
nexttile
plot(t, sqrt(t))
title('root')

examples.title: A flow layout
examples.code:
tiledlayout('flow')
for k = 1:5
    nexttile
    plot(sin(k*linspace(0, pi, 60)))
    title(sprintf('k = %d', k))
end

pages.summary: Keep what is drawn when the next plot is added, or not.
body: By default each plot replaces what the axes show. After `hold on`, plots are added to the axes instead, each taking the next colour, until `hold off`. `hold` alone switches between the two.
syntax: Add later plots to the current axes.
Let the next plot replace what is there.

examples.title: Data, a fit and a marked point in one axes
examples.code:
rng default
x = linspace(0, 3, 30);
y = exp(-x) + 0.05*randn(size(x));
plot(x, y, 'o')
hold on
plot(x, exp(-x), 'LineWidth', 2)
plot(1, exp(-1), 'p', 'MarkerSize', 14, 'MarkerFaceColor', 'y')
hold off
legend('data', 'model', 'x = 1')

body: Text above the axes. A cell array gives several lines. As with labels and legends, `^{…}` and `_{…}` make superscripts and subscripts, and `\alpha` and the other Greek letters, `\pm`, `\circ` and `\infty` their symbols. Name-value pairs set `'FontSize'`, `'FontWeight'`, `'Color'` and the rest.
syntax: With the text object, to change later.

examples.title: A title with symbols, and labels
examples.code:
x = linspace(0, 4*pi, 300);
plot(x, exp(-0.2*x).*sin(x))
title('Damped oscillation: e^{-0.2t} sin(\omega t), \omega = 1')
xlabel('t (s)')
ylabel('amplitude')

examples.title: Two lines, and a larger font
examples.code:
plot(rand(1, 10))
title({'Measurements', 'second series'}, 'FontSize', 14)

pages.summary: The labels of the x, y and z axes.
body: Text beside an axis, usually its quantity and unit. The same TeX symbols as in `title` work here.
syntax: The label of the x axis.
The label of the y axis.
The label of the z axis (for 3-D axes).

examples.title: Labels with units and symbols
examples.code:
T = linspace(250, 350, 50);
plot(T, 101.3*exp(-5000*(1./T - 1/373)))
xlabel('Temperature (K)')
ylabel('Pressure (kPa)')

examples.title: Three axes
examples.code:
[X, Y] = meshgrid(linspace(-1, 1, 20));
surf(X, Y, X.^2 - Y.^2)
xlabel('x')
ylabel('y')
zlabel('x^2 - y^2')

pages.summary: A legend of the plotted objects.
body: A box naming each line or other plotted object, with a sample of how it is drawn. The labels go to the objects in the order they were plotted; a line's `'DisplayName'` gives its label without listing it here. `'Location'` places the box: `'northeast'` (the default), `'northwest'`, `'south'`, `'best'`, and the others named by the compass, or `'...outside'` beyond the axes.
syntax: Labels from the objects' `DisplayName` (or data1, data2, …).
A label for each object, in order.
The labels as a cell array.

examples.title: Labels in order, placed in a corner
Labels from the lines themselves
examples.code:
t = 0:0.1:5;
plot(t, sin(t), 'DisplayName', 'sine')
hold on
plot(t, cos(t), '--', 'DisplayName', 'cosine')
hold off
legend

pages.summary: Set the axis limits and how the axes are shaped.
body: Sets the limits of all axes at once, or a mode: `equal` makes a unit the same length on each axis (a circle looks round), `tight` fits the limits to the data, `square` makes the axes box square, `ij` puts the y origin at the top (as for images), `off` hides the axes. Without arguments it gives the current limits.
syntax: axis([xmin xmax ymin ymax zmin zmax])
axis equal | tight | square | normal | ij | xy | auto | off | on

examples.title: A circle that looks round
Fixed limits, and reading them back

pages.summary: Show or hide the grid lines.
body: Grid lines run across the axes at the tick marks. `grid minor` adds lines between them as well.
syntax: Show, hide, or show with minor lines.
Switch the major grid on or off.

examples.title: Grid lines for reading values
Minor lines on a logarithmic plot
examples.code:
f = logspace(1, 4, 100);
semilogx(f, 20*log10(1 ./ sqrt(1 + (f/1000).^2)))
grid on
grid minor
xlabel('frequency (Hz)')
ylabel('gain (dB)')

pages.summary: The limits of the x, y and z axes.
body: Each sets the lower and upper limit of one axis, leaving the others as they are; without arguments it gives the current limits. `'auto'` lets the axis fit the data again. A limit of `-Inf` or `Inf` keeps that end automatic.
syntax: Back to limits fitted to the data.

examples.title: Zooming in on part of a curve
examples.code:
x = linspace(0, 20, 500);
plot(x, sin(x) ./ x)
xlim([0 10])
ylim([-0.3 1.1])

examples.title: Reading the limits
examples.code:
plot([2 7 4])
lims = ylim

pages.summary: Text at a point of the axes.
body: Places text at the point `(x, y)` in the units of the data, so it moves with the data when the axes are zoomed. By default the text starts at the point and is centred on it vertically; `'HorizontalAlignment'` and `'VerticalAlignment'` move it, and `'FontSize'`, `'Color'` and `'Rotation'` change its look. Several points with a cell array of texts label each one.
syntax: With text properties, and the text objects.

examples.title: Marking points on a curve
examples.code:
x = linspace(0, 2*pi, 100);
plot(x, sin(x))
text(pi/2, 1, '  maximum')
text(3*pi/2, -1, '  minimum')
ylim([-1.3 1.3])

pages.summary: Show the colour scale beside the axes.
body: A bar showing which colour stands for which value, for surfaces, images, contours and scatter plots coloured by value. Its limits follow the axes' colour limits (`clim`). `colorbar off` removes it.
syntax: A colour scale at the right of the axes.
With its handle, to set its `Label` and other properties.

examples.title: The scale of an image
A scale below the axes
examples.code:
contourf(peaks(40), 12)
colorbar('southoutside')

pages.summary: Set or get the colours of the figure's colour scale.
body: The colormap is a list of colours, one row of `[r g b]` per colour, through which surfaces, images and other objects coloured by value pick their colours: the lowest value takes the first row and the highest the last. Named maps include `parula` (the default), `turbo`, `jet`, `hot`, `cool`, `gray` and `bone`; a matrix of your own works too.
syntax: A matrix of colours (values from 0 to 1).
The map of the axes `ax` alone.

examples.title: A named map
examples.code:
surf(peaks(40))
shading interp
colormap hot
colorbar

examples.title: A map for each axes
examples.intro: With axes first, `colormap` sets that axes' map alone.
examples.code:
Z = peaks(60);
subplot(1, 2, 1)
imagesc(Z)
axis image off
colormap(gca, 'parula')
subplot(1, 2, 2)
imagesc(Z)
axis image off
colormap(gca, 'gray')

examples.title: A few distinct colours
examples.code:
imagesc(magic(4))
colormap(turbo(4))
colorbar

body: Closes the current figure, a given one, or all of them. A figure whose `CloseRequestFcn` was set runs that first.

examples.title: Closing some, then all
examples.code:
figure(1); plot(1:3)
figure(2); plot(3:-1:1)
figure(3); plot([1 3 2])
close(2)
open = sort([findobj('Type', 'figure').Number])
close all
remaining = numel(findobj('Type', 'figure'))
